read_locations.book_obligation: Use as dependency comparison. The actual book SR3 calculation must explicitly invoke earlier SR2 distribution and DG4 difference order; no circular use of an abstract ring before SR2.
read_locations.current_batch23_use: Future full-ring order comparison only; not current NP/NL proof evidence.

read_locations.current_batch23_use: Current rational midpoint witness comparison only; established Q operations, not cut field assumptions.

read_locations.book_obligation: Historical attribution only. Do not attribute our P formula, zero branch, common witness, signed distributivity or rational reciprocal proof to an exact passage not found. These are independent book derivations.
read_locations.current_batch23_use: Historical background only; no exact modern strict-cut multiplication proof claimed.

current_batch23_obligations.obligation: Identify positive cuts through zero or a positive rational member; find positive exterior rationals and larger positive interior witnesses using only cut closure/order and Q.

Define P on nonnegative cuts with an independent q<0 branch and positive internal product witnesses. Prove all four cut conditions, nonnegativity, both zero-factor positions, positive products and the zero-product alternative without inverses.

Prove commutation and unit by actual members; 1 is not in i(1), so use a midpoint between q/a and 1. Weak monotonicity inherits witnesses, with zero-factor counterexamples to unjustified strictness/reflection.
For nonnegative rational endpoints separately handle zero; reverse principal-cut product inclusion uses two rational midpoints and legitimate positive divisions, no real square root or inverse.
Nonnegative sums and positive-summand positivity; positive inputs permit larger positive sum/product witnesses even when the given rational member is negative. Zero inputs need separate branches.

Handle zero inputs and negative rational members, then expand both nested products into positive triple witnesses; construct intermediate positive members by rational midpoints in all reverse directions.

Handle all zero inputs; forward inclusion constructs an exact sum after positive witness enlargement. Reverse inclusion allows original sum members of either sign and uses a common max(a1,a2) member before rational distribution. Prove both sides.

Only after NL3, use positive difference D=B⊖A and already-proved additive translation to prove strict monotonicity; total order gives reflection and positive-factor cancellation. No multiplicative surjectivity or inverse existence follows.
